attrs.evidence: holdout_score_core.mjs imports node:fs, node:url and node:path and nothing else -- no canonicaliser, no store, no bundle builder, no checker -- and is invoked over two FILES; js_holdout_adapter.mjs imports the implementation and emits the document; holdout_score.mjs runs each registered adapter as a SEPARATE PROCESS, so a Go adapter enters by exactly the path the JavaScript one does. experiment/fixtures/ carries a synthetic challenge set and observation document containing no TRVM value at all, whose DECLARED result includes a failing arm for all 8 operators and an unresolved arm: a scorer that returned true unconditionally passes the satisfied arm and dies there. The declaration is hand-written and inside experiment_digest, so editing it to agree with a broken scorer moves spec_release_id. Gate `gov-nest`; grid boolean scorer-implementation-free, which reads the import list.
attrs.statement: AN INSTRUMENT WITH NO INPUT MEASURES NOTHING. P4.5 printed `THE SCORER KNOWS EIGHT OPERATORS AND NO TRVM`, which was true of a FUNCTION and false of the PROGRAM: holdout_score.mjs imported cas.mjs, nest_bundle.mjs and nest_check.mjs, and its executable path was always `score(entry, observeJS(entry))`, so nothing that was not this implementation could be scored at all. Deciding after the reveal how a second implementation's observations are shaped, how adapters are invoked, which fields must exist, how an absent field is written and how sets serialise would be adjusting the measuring instrument in the light of the challenges it is about to answer, which is what the preregistration exists to prevent. THE BOUNDARY IS A DOCUMENT, FROZEN BEFORE THE REVEAL: `TRVM-HOLDOUT-OBSERVATION-v1`, with its recipe grammar, observation grammar and JSON schema published in the PROCEDURAL experiment surface rather than as a fourth normative protocol. ONE RESOLUTION ROOT PER OPERATOR AND NO FALLBACK CHAIN, and ABSENT SCORES UNRESOLVED RATHER THAN QUIETLY FALSE.
